did_you_know.text: The chapter opens with two parallel questions: Who may dwell in the Lord’s tent, and who may live on His holy mountain? Together, they ask who is worthy to be in the Lord’s presence.
The verse describes the worthy person in three ways: he walks with integrity, does what is right, and speaks the truth from his heart.
Moral integrity also includes the use of speech: the person described does not slander, harm his neighbor, or bring disgrace on someone close to him.
The verse connects speech with social responsibility: it is not enough to avoid lying; one must also avoid gossip, causing harm, and humiliating others.
The worthy person does not value people solely according to their status: he despises those who are morally contemptible and honors those who fear the Lord.
The verse emphasizes faithfulness to one’s commitments: a person who makes an oath does not break his word, even when keeping it brings hardship or personal cost.
Integrity is also expressed in financial matters: the person described does not lend money at interest or accept a bribe against the innocent.
The chapter ends with a general promise: whoever does all these things will never be shaken; his way will be stable and secure.
